findings.summary: AxiosError.from no longer copies the original error's own properties (errno, syscall, address, port), drops the old message/name 'Error' fallbacks, throws a TypeError on null/undefined error, and treats a falsy code differently from the old `code == null` check.
`cause` is now an enumerable own property, where it used to be non-enumerable on purpose to keep JSON and log output clean.
`this.status = response.status` drops the old `null` fallback, so a response with no status gives `undefined` instead of `null`.
`isAxiosError` is now an own, enumerable, writable property. It used to be a non-enumerable property on the prototype.
Static error codes (ERR_*, ECONNABORTED, ETIMEDOUT) were non-writable and non-enumerable. They are now ordinary assignable properties and can be overwritten.
`__CANCEL__` moved from the prototype to an enumerable own property on every instance, so it shows up in Object.keys and equality assertions.
Both classes now require `new`, so third-party code using `AxiosError.call(this, ...)` with `utils.inherits` throws 'Class constructor cannot be invoked without new'.
